scope: Caller-separated native protein-altering allele inventory and descriptive genotype/consequence models; no phenotype score or EPCR.

quality_handling.interpretation: Diagnostic bins inherited from the earlier supplied-VCF screen. Missing and unfiltered remain explicit; these bins are not a newly validated sensitivity or ranking policy.

frequency.source: gnomAD exome and genome population allele counts in retained Exomiser 2512 public allele database
frequency.calculation: Maximum AC/AN fraction over available populations with valid positive AN; use counts, not an unset protobuf frequency field
frequency.missing: Separate frequency-unresolved group; absence or AN=0 is not AF=0
frequency.quality_caveat: Database counts do not establish site quality or population callability; investigate candidates separately

limitations: Only the selected completed autosomal snapshot is represented. Pending or outside-scope chromosomes and absent variant records are not callable-reference evidence.

Every selected concrete protein-altering allele row is retained, including uncalled ALT, unfiltered or named-filter records, and missing/low quality. These are review inventories, not quality-passing findings.
Original caller, source hash and record ordinal distinguish duplicate records. Full native GT/ALT/FORMAT/PL/AD and rendered record remain authoritative over recoded normalized rows.
Ordinary descriptive recessive models require fully called diploid sequence genotypes and noncolliding normalized keys; excluded structures and cis/overlap pairs remain review evidence.
Quality bins DP10/GQ20 are historical diagnostics only. No PASS label or genotype-quality score is imputed, and no quality threshold or clinical precision/recall is newly validated.
Local consequence annotations do not infer joint coding haplotypes, parental phase, clinical pathogenicity or proven loss of function.
Models are caller-separated; source genotype/block phase assertions are not independent validation or parental-origin evidence. Conflicting phase annotations remain unresolved.
Missing public frequency information is not zero. Valid observed counts and source denominators remain visible; population observations do not themselves establish pathogenicity.
Partial-snapshot model lists are not complete-genome rankings or EPCR estimates and must be reconciled after calling finishes.
This autosomal coding review does not replace X/Y, mitochondrial, structural, copy-number, repeat, regulatory, mosaic, callability or phenotype analysis.
